## assistant

The commit button works again, and the message now follows your prompt.

**Cause.** The generation call goes through Pi's `modelRuntime.completeSimple` directly, which skips the per-request headers Pi's own agent loop adds. Your current model is on the OpenCode "Console Go" provider, and its gateway rejects any request without the `x-opencode-session` header, so the button failed with "Request is missing x-opencode-session" while normal chat on the same model kept working. It was not a git problem: my first repro of "Extension is not installed: git" came from a mangled path in my own test script, and the git extension itself is fine.

**Fix.** The commit-message routine now lives in its own server module. It passes the thread's session id and the OpenCode session header on the request, uses your prompt verbatim as the system prompt with the extension's diff as the user message, and allows a longer reply so a wrapped body is not cut off. Verified end to end against the live server on this repo's working tree: the result came back with a lowercase prefix, present tense, and 72-column wrapping.

**Server.** Since this morning Gizmo runs under the genge-services supervisor, not the old launcher. The fix is live: I restarted the supervised process and the supervisor brought it back healthy. I briefly added a log line to the git extension in your registry to chase the false lead and have reverted it; the registry tree is clean.

**Not committed.** All of today's work, including this fix, is still uncommitted in the working tree. Server tests pass with a new test for the header logic, and the worklog has an entry.
